title: Internal and sectionwise module inverse images agree for a geometric morphism
statement:
Let $C,D$ be sites small in a common coefficient universe [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-size-convention]. On each site assume abelian sheafification exists and its local equivalences are monoidal, and use the sheafified objectwise tensor over $\mathbf Z$ [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. Let $u:\operatorname{Sh}(D)\to\operatorname{Sh}(C)$ be a geometric morphism [def-trf-geometric-morphism]. Write $L=u^{-1}$ on sets and on abelian sheaves, using the induced finite-product lift on algebraic operations. Give the abelian lift the canonical strong monoidal structure obtained by inverting the oplax structure which is mate, under $L\dashv u_*$, to the canonical lax structure on $u_*$ induced by the sheafified tensor. Write $\mu^L$ for its tensorator. Then $\mu^L_{A,B}:LA\otimes LB\to L(A\otimes B)$ agrees with the map induced by the set inverse image of the universal bilinear pairing $A\times B\to A\otimes B$ and the inverse product comparison; the unit map agrees with that induced by inverse image of the constant integer section $1$.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring object of $\operatorname{Sh}(C,\operatorname{Ab})$ and put $S=L(R)$ with this transported ring structure [sk-def-sfb-transport]. Let $R_{\mathrm{sec}},S_{\mathrm{sec}}$ and $E_R,E_S$ denote reconstructed section-ring sheaves and internal/sectionwise module equivalences [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]. Let $L_{R_{\mathrm{sec}}}$ be inverse image of sectionwise module sheaves: it applies $L$ to underlying sheaves, ring operations and scalar action using the inverse finite-product comparison [def-weil-pbc-algebraic-inverse-image]. There are a canonical ring-sheaf isomorphism and a natural module-sheaf isomorphism
$$\sigma_R:S_{\mathrm{sec}}\xrightarrow{\sim}L(R_{\mathrm{sec}}),\qquad
\theta_M:E_S(\operatorname{mapMod}(L)M)\xrightarrow{\sim}L_{R_{\mathrm{sec}}}(E_RM),$$
where the second is semilinear over $\sigma_R$. Under the canonical comparisons of underlying inverse-image sheaves, both maps are identities. In particular $\sigma_R$ intertwines addition, zero, multiplication and one, and $\theta_M$ intertwines addition and the scalar action $L(\gamma_M)\circ\mu^L_{R,M}$ with the finite-product inverse image of the sectionwise scalar action. Applied termwise to any unbounded cochain complex $P$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], these maps give an isomorphism of complexes over $\sigma_R$, natural in $P$, intertwining each differential with $L(d_P)$; hence also an isomorphism of their images in the derived category. No K-flatness, termwise flatness or enough-points hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 03D2, lemma-pullback-module: finite-product inverse image of scalar actions. The comparison with internal monoidal transport is the extracted argument of the parent proof step 2; supplementary algebraic-lift and tensor references are recorded in report.md.

proof.text:
Write $G=u_*$, $\eta,\epsilon$ for the set adjunction unit and counit, and $\lambda_{A,B}:L(A\times B)\cong LA\times LB$, $\rho_{H,K}:G(H\times K)\cong GH\times GK$ for the product comparisons, with $\lambda_*,\rho_*$ their terminal-object versions. The right adjoint preserves these products [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-limits]; the supplied lifted adjunction, its unit_eq, and [def-trf-abelian-inverse-image-presentation] identify the underlying unit and transpose formulas. Write $p_{A,B}:A\times B\to A\otimes B$ for the universal bilinear pairing. The universal property of the integer tensor product, extended by the sheafification adjunction, applies to the sheafified objectwise tensor [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]: additivity is integer linearity, and sectionwise maps extend uniquely through sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Unpack the canonical lax structure on $G$: its tensor map $m_{H,K}$ is the unique additive sheaf extension of the bilinear map $G(p_{H,K})\rho_{H,K}^{-1}$; its unit $e:\mathbf Z_C\to G\mathbf Z_D$ extends $n\mapsto n\,G(1_D)\rho_*^{-1}$. Product preservation carries the separate-additivity equations to those of this pairing. Thus
$$m_{H,K}p_{GH,GK}=G(p_{H,K})\rho_{H,K}^{-1},\qquad e1_C=G(1_D)\rho_*^{-1}.$$
These are extension formulas for sheafified tensors, not a claim that arbitrary sections of a tensor sheaf are pure tensors. Lean construction: tensorPresheafLift uses TensorProduct.liftAddHom; tensorLift extends it through sheafificationAdjunction and the canonical strong tensor comparison. tensor_ext and tensor_ext3 descend the tensor uniqueness tests through sheafification, without assuming pure tensors generate all sheaf sections globally. unitLift and unit_ext use the sheafified constant integer presheaf. transportedPairing_graph and transportedPairing_add_left/right construct the finite-product transport, and its universal sections prove associativity, unitality and symmetry. normalization_unique fixes the resulting lax structure. Right additivity follows from left additivity and symmetry. The triple tensor test is justified by the monoidality of local equivalences and the sheaf property of its target. The right-unit law follows from the left-unit law and braiding.

proof.text:
Let $d_{A,B}:L(A\otimes B)\to LA\otimes LB$ be the specified oplax tensor comparison. By its definition as mate [lem-sfb-monoidal-adjunction-mates], its abelian adjunct is $m_{LA,LB}(\eta_A\otimes\eta_B)$, so
$$G(d_{A,B})\eta_{A\otimes B}p_{A,B}=G(p_{LA,LB})\rho_{LA,LB}^{-1}(\eta_A\times\eta_B).$$
Here naturality of $p$ and step 1 give the equality. Naturality of the unit with the two projections gives
$$\rho_{LA,LB}\,G(\lambda_{A,B})\eta_{A\times B}=\eta_A\times\eta_B.$$
Also $\eta_{A\otimes B}p_{A,B}=G(Lp_{A,B})\eta_{A\times B}$. Consequently the first equation says that the two maps $d_{A,B}Lp_{A,B}$ and $p_{LA,LB}\lambda_{A,B}$ have the same adjunct under the SET adjunction. Its injective Hom bijection gives
$$d_{A,B}Lp_{A,B}=p_{LA,LB}\lambda_{A,B}.$$
The use of the set adjunction is legitimate even though $p$ is not additive on the product: the supplied lifted adjunction, its unit_eq, and [def-trf-abelian-inverse-image-presentation] identify the unit used in the abelian mate formula with the original set unit. Now $d_{A,B}$ is invertible. Applying $L$ and $\lambda$ to the separate-additivity equations of $p_{A,B}$ shows that $L(p_{A,B})\lambda_{A,B}^{-1}$ is separately additive for the lifted group laws $L(+)\lambda^{-1}$, so by step 1 it equals $\varphi\,p_{LA,LB}$ for a unique additive $\varphi$. Then $d\varphi p_{LA,LB}=dL(p)\lambda^{-1}=p_{LA,LB}$, so $d\varphi=1$ by uniqueness. Additive $\alpha,\beta:L(A\otimes B)\to T$ are equal iff their adjuncts $G(\alpha)\eta,G(\beta)\eta$ agree after $p_{A,B}$ (step 1), i.e. iff $\alpha L(p)=\beta L(p)$ by set injectivity; as $\varphi dL(p)=\varphi p\lambda=L(p)$, $\varphi d=1$. By definition $\mu^L_{A,B}=d_{A,B}^{-1}=\varphi$, and cancellation yields
$$\mu^L_{A,B}p_{LA,LB}=L(p_{A,B})\lambda_{A,B}^{-1}.$$
This also constructs the required induced additive map: it is $\mu^L$ itself, and the tensor universal property in step 1 gives uniqueness. In Lean, tensor_graph_of_normalization reads the tensor graph equation directly from the normalization on the universal product.

source.place: Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback: adjunction and the universal bilinear pairing; explicit mate normalization

proof.text:
For the oplax unit $d_0:L\mathbf Z_C\to\mathbf Z_D$, [lem-sfb-monoidal-adjunction-mates] gives $G(d_0)\eta_{\mathbf Z_C}=e$. Naturality at the set map $1_C:*_C\to|\mathbf Z_C|$, step 1 and terminal-object uniqueness give
$$G(d_0L1_C)\eta_{*_C}=e1_C=G(1_D)\rho_*^{-1}=G(1_D\lambda_*)\eta_{*_C}.$$
Injectivity of the set adjunction therefore gives $d_0L1_C=1_D\lambda_*$. Moreover $d_0$ is invertible: let $\varphi_0:\mathbf Z_D\to L\mathbf Z_C$ be the additive map with $\varphi_01_D=L(1_C)\lambda_*^{-1}$ (unique by the next paragraph). Then $d_0\varphi_01_D=1_D$, so $d_0\varphi_0=1$. Additive maps $L\mathbf Z_C\to T$ are determined by their adjuncts under the supplied lifted adjunction; unit_eq and [def-trf-abelian-inverse-image-presentation] identify these adjuncts on underlying sheaves, and they are determined by their value on $1_C$, hence by precomposition with $L1_C$ (set injectivity); since $\varphi_0d_0L1_C=\varphi_01_D\lambda_*=L1_C$, $\varphi_0d_0=1$. Inverting $d_0$ gives the claimed unit formula
$$(d_0^{-1})1_D=L(1_C)\lambda_*^{-1}.$$
An additive sheaf map out of $\mathbf Z_D$ is determined by this section: on the constant integer presheaf it must send $n$ to $n$ times that section, and [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] extends this map uniquely. Thus this is exactly the unit map induced by inverse image of $1$, including its sheafification normalization. In Lean, unit_graph_of_normalization reads the unit graph equation directly from normalization on the terminal sheaf.

proof.text:
Let $b_R:R\otimes R\to R$ and $v_R:\mathbf Z_C\to R$ be the internal multiplication and unit, and put $a_R=b_Rp_{R,R}$, $1_R=v_R1_C$. By [def-sfb-modobj-transport], the transported multiplication and unit are $L(b_R)\mu^L_{R,R}$ and $L(v_R)d_0^{-1}$. Reconstruct the section ring using [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]. Steps 2 and 3 identify its multiplication and one with
$$L(b_R)\mu^L_{R,R}p_{LR,LR}=L(a_R)\lambda_{R,R}^{-1},\qquad L(v_R)d_0^{-1}1_D=L(1_R)\lambda_*^{-1}.$$
Addition and zero are $L(+)\lambda^{-1}$ and $L(0)\lambda_*^{-1}$ by the graph equations of [def-trf-abelian-inverse-image-presentation]. These are precisely the operations of the algebraic inverse image [def-weil-pbc-algebraic-inverse-image]. The canonical underlying comparison therefore preserves addition, zero, multiplication and one; its inverse does too. It defines $\sigma_R$, the identity after the stated underlying-sheaf identifications. The private graph_compare_add and graph_compare_bilinear lemmas share the generalized-section calculation for the ring and module comparisons.

source.place: Tag 03D2, lemma-pullback-module; Tag 03EK; sites.tex Tag 00YV, ring operations

proof.text:
For an internal module $M$, write $\gamma_M:R\otimes M\to M$ for its action and $a_M=\gamma_Mp_{R,M}$ for the corresponding sectionwise bilinear action. This correspondence follows from the universal property of the integer tensor product and the sheafification adjunction; the module associativity and unit identities become $(rs)m=r(sm)$ and $1m=m$ upon precomposition with the universal pairings, so this is the section action in the canonical equivalence. [def-sfb-modobj-transport] gives the transported action $L(\gamma_M)\mu^L_{R,M}$. Its reconstructed section action, by step 2, is
$$L(\gamma_M)\mu^L_{R,M}p_{LR,LM}=L(a_M)\lambda_{R,M}^{-1}.$$
This is the scalar action specified by [def-weil-pbc-algebraic-inverse-image]. Additions agree by the abelian lift as in step 4. The identity on the common underlying inverse-image abelian sheaf is therefore additive and semilinear over $\sigma_R$; the same identity is its inverse. It gives $\theta_M$ using the unchanged underlying sheaves of [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]. On every module morphism $h$, both functors have underlying map $L(h)$, by the two cited transport definitions and the canonical section equivalence. Hence $\theta$ is natural.

source.place: Tag 03D2, lemma-pullback-module, action and functoriality; Tag 03EK universal pairing

proof.text:
Apply step 5 to every $P^n$ and to the module map $d_P^n:P^n\to P^{n+1}$. Naturality gives
$$\theta_{P^{n+1}}\,E_S(\operatorname{mapMod}(L)(d_P^n))=L_{R_{\mathrm{sec}}}(E_R(d_P^n))\,\theta_{P^n}.$$
Under the common underlying-sheaf identifications, both differential maps are $L(d_P^n)$. Thus these components and their inverses are chain maps and give the asserted isomorphism of unbounded complexes over $\sigma_R$, natural in $P$. Identify the coefficient categories through $\sigma_R$; applying the localization functor $Q$ of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] to these mutually inverse chain maps gives mutually inverse morphisms in the derived category. This last assertion concerns the images of the displayed complexes and needs no resolution, no derived tensor calculation and no assertion about preserving arbitrary quasi-isomorphisms. All preceding equations are identities of sheaf maps, so no bound, flatness or enough-points assumption has entered.
